title: NY Steak, Seared Then Sliced (RECIPE - draft)

NY Steak, Seared Then Sliced (gf). Same reverse-sear method and portion approach as Ribeye Steak, Seared Then Sliced -- tempered, seasoned salt/pepper/garlic powder/rosemary, baked on rack over sheet pan, rested, then high-heat seared and sliced on-site for full service.

METHOD (reduced time/temp vs. Ribeye, confirmed w/ Sandra 2026-08-30):
1. Temper 10 min at room temp.
2. Season both sides: salt, pepper, garlic powder, rosemary.
3. Bake at 250F for 20 min (vs. ribeye's 30 min) or until 85F internal (vs. ribeye's 90F).
4. Remove from oven, set aside.
5. Sear high heat until ~110F internal (vs. ribeye's ~120F) -- NY strip cooks/toughens faster than ribeye, so pulled at a lower sear temp.

SLICE: on-site for full service, same rationale as ribeye (avoid overcooking from hot-box carryover).

title: Beef Goulash, Braised w/ Red Wine, Paprika, Carrots, Onion (RECIPE)
content:
Beef Goulash, Braised w/ Red Wine, Paprika, Carrots, Onion (gf). Follows the Beef Bourguignon method closely -- see that entry for the base. Differences: no bacon, double the paprika, plus cumin and bay leaf.

BEEF: Costco beef stew meat, pre-cubed ~1 oz cubes. Sear in olive oil, high heat, salt + pepper, a couple minutes, pull off heat, set aside. (No bacon step -- olive oil only.)

STEW BASE (into pressure cooker): seared beef + 1 can diced tomatoes (unseasoned) + thyme, oregano, salt, pepper, rosemary (by feel) + paprika + cumin (ratio: 1.5 tsp cumin per 1 tsp paprika, paprika itself double the Bourguignon's amount) + 1-2 bay leaves + several cups red wine (by feel) + chicken bouillon + water, enough to fully submerge.

COOK: pressure cooker, ~2 hours (sometimes longer), until beef is fork-tender.

CARROTS & ONION (kept separate from pressure cook, same technique as Short Ribs): saute onion + carrots separately. NOT added to the pressure cooker -- held aside, added at reheat/service so they stay firm rather than going mushy.

Confirmed w/ Sandra 2026-08-30.

title: Sea Bass, Pan Seared, Butter, Lemon, Caper (RECIPE)
page_body:
SEA BASS, PAN SEARED, BUTTER, LEMON, CAPER (gf).

PORTION: 4-5 oz filet per person (same as Onion & Olive Herbed Tomato Reduction variant).

SEA BASS (same base sear method as Onion & Olive variant):
1. Season filet lightly with salt on both sides, light pepper.
2. Saute in butter, 2 tbsp per filet.
3. Add garlic, saute 1 min.
4. Turn filet, saute 1 min other side.
5. Reduce heat to low, add white wine to cover half the height of the filet.
6. Cover with lid, simmer/cook, flip occasionally. If pan runs dry, add more white wine.
7. As the filet approaches 135F internal: add ~1 tsp fresh-squeezed lemon juice + capers, baste the fish with the pan liquid.
8. Pull at 135F internal.

No onion/tomato/olive reduction on this variant -- finish is just the butter/wine/lemon/caper pan sauce, basted.

Confirmed w/ Sandra 2026-08-30.

title: Moussaka Eggplant Casserole -- Beef (RECIPE)
content:
MOUSSAKA EGGPLANT CASSEROLE -- BEEF (gf). Shares eggplant prep, marinara, potato layer, bechamel, and bake with the Vegetarian version -- only the filling layer differs. See sibling: Moussaka Eggplant Casserole -- Vegetarian.

EGGPLANT PREP (shared step):
1. Slice eggplant 1/4-1/2 inch thick.
2. Lay on paper towel, salt one side by hand, let sit a few minutes, dab off sweat/moisture.
3. Flip, salt other side, let sit, dab both sides well.
4. Griddle on flat surface, low heat. Brush each side generously with olive oil (eggplant absorbs a lot). Season each side with garlic salt + Italian seasoning. Flip and repeat oiling/seasoning as needed until soft to the touch. Remove, set aside.

- Once hot, add ground beef: 5 lb
- Salt and pepper
- Cook thoroughly, let cool before assembly

ASSEMBLY (2 layers + top, confirmed order):
1. Sliced parboiled potato, covered with marinara.
2. Eggplant slices over potato.
3. Beef filling over eggplant.
4. Ricotta dolloped over beef, smeared/spread.
5. Thin layer shredded mozzarella.
6. Repeat the full stack (potato+marinara -> eggplant -> beef -> ricotta -> mozzarella) for layer 2.
7. Top layer: eggplant, marinara, cheeses.
8. Bechamel: pour over top layer to cover completely (see Bechamel, Gluten-Free entry). Refrigerate to firm up.

BAKE: cover with parchment, bake 395F for 30 min, remove parchment, bake 7 more min uncovered.

title: Bechamel, Gluten-Free (SAUCE)
page_body:
BECHAMEL (gluten-free house version). Reusable across dishes -- Sandra flagged this for reuse beyond Moussaka.

INGREDIENTS:
- Butter: 1 stick (8 tbsp)
- Olive oil: 2 tbsp
- Gluten-free flour: 1 tbsp to start, add more a little at a time until batter-like consistency (Sandra judges by feel/texture)
- Half & half, or heavy cream watered down: added hot, in small additions -- MUST be hot or sauce clumps
- Salt & pepper: to taste, any point

METHOD:
1. Melt butter, add olive oil, heat.
2. Add GF flour, stir. Add more flour a little at a time if needed until batter-like consistency is reached.
3. Add hot half & half (or watered-down heavy cream) a little at a time, stirring continuously -- never walk away, it clumps if liquid isn't hot or if not stirred continuously.
4. Continue adding liquid + stirring until sauce reaches a thick bechamel consistency.
5. Salt and pepper to taste at any point.

Confirmed w/ Sandra 2026-08-29 (captured during Moussaka interview).

title: RULE: Carryover Cooking in Hot-Box Transport (target IT set below final-eat temp)
page_body:
Meat/fish target internal temps in Taza recipes are deliberately set below final-eating-temp guidance in some cases, because the product continues to cook (carryover) while held in hot boxes during transport to the event. Pulling at a lower IT prevents the protein from overcooking/toughening by the time it's served at the buffet. This is intentional technique, not an error or food-safety gap -- confirmed w/ Sandra 2026-08-29 (raised re: Za'atar Lamb Pops, 129F pull vs 145F+rest standard guidance).

APPLIES TO: any protein that (a) travels in a hot box before service and (b) is meant to be served medium/medium-rare or otherwise benefits from a moist finish (lamb pops confirmed; salmon's 135F pull temp, set the same session, likely follows the same logic -- not yet explicitly confirmed as carryover-driven, flag to re-check).

OPERATIONAL IMPLICATION: when locking a new recipe's target IT, ask whether the pulled/plated number already accounts for hot-box carryover, or is the true food-safety-relevant final temp. Don't assume a lower-than-USDA-standard IT is a mistake -- verify with Sandra before flagging or overwriting it.

7. Bake at 375F until chicken reaches 165F internal.

title: Lemon Feta Spinach Reduction (SAUCE)
content:
LEMON FETA SPINACH REDUCTION. Used on: Greek Feta Chicken Breast (topped after baking).

RATIOS (confirmed w/ Sandra 2026-08-29):
- Butter: 4-6 tbsp
- Olive oil: ~1 tsp
- Gluten-free flour: up to ~2 tbsp
- Chicken bouillon powder: to taste
- Hot water: up to 1 cup
- Fresh lemon juice: 3-4 tbsp
- Salt: to taste (light -- feta adds salt later)
- Feta, crumbled: 1/2 cup
- Fresh spinach, chopped: 1-2 cups

METHOD:
1. Melt butter in saute pan.
2. Add olive oil.
3. Add GF flour -- just enough that it's fully absorbed and mixture thickens (roux).
4. Add chicken bouillon powder, mix in.
5. Add hot water a little at a time, continuously mixing, to avoid clumping. Sauce thins as more water is added -- keep adding/mixing until desired thickness reached (up to 1 cup water total).
6. Add fresh-squeezed lemon juice.
7. Add salt to taste -- light.
8. Add crumbled feta + chopped fresh spinach, stir through.
9. Pour over baked chicken. Ready to pack for delivery or full service.

Source: 2026-08-29 interview.

title: Beef Bourguignon (RECIPE - draft)
content:
Beef Bourguignon (NOT halal by default -- see halal mod below).

BEEF: Costco beef stew meat, pre-cubed ~1 oz cubes. Sear in olive oil, high heat, salt + pepper, a couple minutes, then pull off heat and set aside.

BACON: ~1 pack (12-16 slices), diced small, cooked in a saucepan until partially cooked. Rendered fat is used to saute the onion (below). Partially-cooked bacon pieces go into the pressure cooker with the beef.

ONION (kept separate from pressure cook): saute in the reserved bacon fat until translucent. Do NOT add to the pressure cooker -- held aside and added only at reheat/service time, so it stays firm rather than going mushy.

STEW BASE (into pressure cooker): seared beef + partially-cooked bacon + 1 can diced tomatoes (unseasoned) + thyme, oregano, salt, pepper, rosemary, paprika (seasoned by feel) + several cups red wine (by feel) + chicken bouillon + water, enough to fully submerge.

COOK: pressure cooker, 2 hours (sometimes longer). Done when beef is fork-tender/flakes -- judged by texture, not a fixed IT.

SERVICE/REHEAT: sauteed onion is stirred in fresh at reheat, not cooked in the pressure cooker.

HALAL MODIFICATION: bacon is simply omitted for halal portions, no substitute added.

Confirmed w/ Sandra 2026-08-30.

title: Beef Short Ribs (RECIPE)
content:
Braised Herbed Short Ribs. Bone-in short ribs, seared then braised low-and-slow. Sandra's recipe. Standard practice: cooked T-1 (day before), reheated day-of.

SOURCE/PREP: purchased from WinCo, precut bone-in, cut into individual pieces. Temper 15 min at room temp (out of fridge) before searing.

SEAR: sear with oil. Generous handful of Gyro Seasoning (dry mix) + salt sprinkled on one side to fully cover, sear until browned, flip -- brown a second side (unseasoned), flip -- season second side same way (Gyro Seasoning + salt), sear until browned, flip -- brown fourth side (unseasoned). Net: all 4 sides seared/browned, 2 opposite sides seasoned directly.

BRAISE (T-1, day before): seared ribs into full-size hotel pan (~36+ pieces per full pan). Add red wine + water + chicken bouillon (3 tsp per 3 cups water) + rosemary + salt -- quantities scale by feel to however much is in the pan. Cover with parchment paper, then foil over that. Bake at 425F for 3.5-4 hours (full pan, 36+ pieces) until falling off bone.

REHEAT/FINISH (day-of): keep parchment + foil cover on, reheat 1 hour. Separately, saute 2 onions (chunked) + precut carrot sticks, seasoned w/ Italian seasoning + garlic salt. Add the sauteed onion/carrot to the pan during the reheat period. Ribs + vegetables come out together, ready to pack for buffet transport.

PORTIONING/SALES: Platter Collection (delivery/setup) sells as 8 pieces per half-pan. Full-service catering sells by headcount -- batch size scales to party size.

SAUCE: no separate reduction sauce mentioned across two full walkthroughs -- the braising liquid (red wine/water/bouillon/rosemary) reduces naturally over the ~4.5-5 total hrs of covered bake + reheat and serves as the pan jus. Not explicitly confirmed as intentional vs. just how it turns out -- flag if precision matters here.

Child procedures: Sear, Braise, Reheat/Finish, Pack.
